answer: A public webcam overlooking a square publishes its view every minute, and a claimant must submit a photo taken from the same square showing the same crowd, weather and light at that minute, with yarrow growing by the railings. No fable about visiting in sunshine survives if the webcam shows rain, a velvet awning cannot hide the strangers in the frame, and a relic of an old photo cannot predict the scene, so a farm needs someone at every camera-covered square.
